title: CPIB Investigation Involving Minister S Iswaran and the Resignations of Former Speaker and a PAP MP
what_it_is: CPIB Investigation Involving Minister S Iswaran and the Resignations of Former Speaker and a PAP MP

sections.label: CPIB Iswaran investigation facts
sections.summary: CPIB found information on Minister Iswaran while investigating a separate matter and alerted the speaker on 29 May.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: On the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB) investigation involving Minister Iswaran, briefly, the facts of the case are these: while investigating a separate matter, the CPIB came across some information concerning Minister Iswaran that merited investigation.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: CPIB alerted me on 29 May and pursued this lead further on their own volition.

sections.label: Iswaran interdicted with reduced pay
sections.summary: Minister Iswaran was interdicted from duty with reduced pay of $8,500 per month until further notice.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Subsequently, I interdicted Minister Iswaran from duty with a reduced pay of $8,500 per month, until further notice.

sections.label: Tan and Cheng affair continued
sections.summary: Information suggested the affair continued, so Mr Tan had to go and Miss Cheng had to resign.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: A few weeks ago, I came across information that strongly suggested that the affair had continued.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: I decided that Mr Tan had to go forthwith.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Miss Cheng had to resign too because she had not broken off the affair even after being told to stop.

sections.label: Tan and Cheng did not stop
sections.summary: Mr Tan and Miss Cheng did not stop the affair and both had to go, and the speaker should have forced the issue earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Regrettably, in the end, Mr Tan and Miss Cheng did not stop the affair, and both had to go.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: On reflection, as I said, I should have forced the issue earlier, certainly before mid-term.

sections.label: Ridout Road rentals ministers exonerated
sections.summary: The two Ministers involved in Ridout Road rentals were thoroughly investigated, including by CPIB, and fully exonerated.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: With the Ridout Road rentals, when allegations of preferential treatment surfaced, the two Ministers involved were thoroughly investigated, including by CPIB, and eventually fully exonerated.

sections.label: Zero tolerance for corruption suspicion
sections.summary: There is zero tolerance when there is suspicion or allegation of wrongdoing in official duties, especially possible corruption.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: One, when there is a suspicion or allegation of wrongdoing in the discharge of official duties, especially possible corruption, there is zero tolerance.

sections.label: Past corruption cases political office holders
sections.summary: Singapore has seen past corruption cases involving political office holders Tan Kia Gan, Wee Toon Boon, Teh Cheang Wan and Phey Yew Kok.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Singapore has seen corruption cases involving political office holders in the past: Mr Tan Kia Gan in 1966, he was then Minister for National Development; Mr Wee Toon Boon in 1975, he was then a Minister of State, I think in the Ministry of Defence  ; Mr Teh Cheang Wan in 1986, he was Minister for National Development; and earlier in 1979, Mr Phey Yew Kok, then President of NTUC and also an MP.

sections.label: Former Speaker and MP affair
sections.summary: The extramarital affair between the former Speaker and former MP should not have happened.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: For example, the extramarital affair between the former Speaker and former MP should not have happened.

sections.label: Forcing the issue earlier
sections.summary: Looking back, the speaker would have forced the issue earlier if able to do it again.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Looking back, if I could do it again, I would have forced the issue earlier.

sections.label: Carrying through what needs doing
sections.summary: For the good of the country, what needs to be done will be carried through according to the law, even if embarrassing.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: For the good of our country, we will carry through what needs to be done in accordance with the law, even if it may be politically embarrassing and painful to the party.

sections.label: Upholding standards after PAP hit
sections.summary: With the Iswaran investigation and resignations, the PAP has taken a hit but will uphold standards and do the right thing.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: With the investigation into Minister Iswaran, and the resignations of the Speaker and an MP, the PAP has taken a hit, but we will show Singaporeans that we will uphold standards and do the right thing, so that trust is maintained, and the Singapore system continues to work well.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: This is my approach, and I am confident it will be my successor’s approach too, and this is how we will keep Singapore safe, strong and prosperous for many years to come.

sections.label: Questions on CPIB investigation timelines
sections.summary: Several Members posed questions on timelines and circumstances of CPIB investigations involving Minister Iswaran and initial Government statements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Several Members – Dr Tan Wu Meng, Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Leong Mun Wai, Mr Gerald Giam and Mr Dennis Tan – have posed questions relating to timelines and circumstances surrounding the CPIB investigations involving Minister Iswaran, and on the information put out in the initial statements by the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: I must emphasise that what information to put out on ongoing investigations are operational judgement calls that law enforcement agencies take.

sections.label: CPIB discloses Iswaran investigation
sections.summary: CPIB decided to disclose on 12 July that Minister Iswaran was assisting investigations into a case CPIB uncovered.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In Minister Iswaran’s case, given that it involved a Minister, CPIB decided to disclose on 12 July that Minister Iswaran was assisting CPIB with investigations into a case uncovered by CPIB.

sections.label: CPIB confirms arrests
sections.summary: CPIB judged it appropriate at that point to confirm that Mr Ong and Minister Iswaran had been arrested.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: CPIB made the operational judgement call that it would be appropriate at that point in time to confirm that both Mr Ong and Minister Iswaran had been arrested.

sections.label: Prime Minister consent for CPIB investigation
sections.summary: CPIB kept the Prime Minister informed and sought his concurrence to investigate Minister Iswaran, a Cabinet Minister.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In this case, it kept the Prime Minister informed and sought his concurrence to initiate formal investigations of Minister Iswaran because the investigations concerned a Cabinet Minister.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Under Article 22G of the Constitution, in the event the Prime Minister refuses to give his consent to a CPIB investigation, the Director of CPIB can go directly to the elected President for his or her concurrence to proceed with the investigation.

sections.label: Difference between CPIB investigations
sections.summary: Mr Don Wee asked why Ministers Shanmugam and Vivian continued duties while investigated, and there is a crucial difference from the Iswaran investigation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Mr Don Wee asked why Minister Shanmugam and Minister Vivian continued with their duties while being investigated by CPIB on the Ridout Road bungalow issue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: There is a crucial difference between that earlier CPIB investigation into Ministers Shanmugam and Vivian, and CPIB's ongoing investigation involving Minister Iswaran.

sections.label: Iswaran suspended from duties
sections.summary: The Prime Minister assessed that it was necessary to suspend Minister Iswaran from his official duties during the investigation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In these circumstances, the Prime Minister's assessment was that it was necessary to suspend Minister Iswaran from his official duties while the investigation took place.

sections.label: Leave of absence effected
sections.summary: The leave of absence arising from the CPIB investigation was effected only on 12 July.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The leave of absence arising from the CPIB investigation was effected only on 12 July.

sections.label: Code of Conduct for Ministers
sections.summary: The Code of Conduct for Ministers has existed since 1954 and was last updated in 2005.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Code of Conduct for Ministers has been in place since 1954 and was last updated in 2005.

sections.label: Anonymous source investigation cases
sections.summary: Of 83 cases registered for investigation in 2022, 13 cases, about 16%, came from anonymous sources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Of the 83 cases registered for investigation in 2022, 13 cases – or about 16% – were from anonymous sources.

sections.label: Retaining gifts by officers
sections.summary: Officers may retain gifts below $50 if integrity is unaffected; gifts above $50 require paying assessed market value to the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Officers may be allowed to retain gifts that are valued below $50 if doing so does not affect the integrity of the Civil Service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: If officers wish to retain gifts valued above $50, they must pay the assessed market value of the gift to the Government.

sections.label: Declaring meal invitations
sections.summary: Civil servants should declare and seek Permanent Secretaries' approval for meal invitations before the meal or immediately after if not possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In such instances, civil servants should declare and seek approval from their Permanent Secretaries if they receive any meal invitation either before the meal or, if that is not possible, immediately after.

sections.label: Refusing and returning gifts
sections.summary: All gifts should generally be refused and returned to the donor without delay; political office holders retaining a gift must pay the Government the valuation price.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In general, all gifts should be refused and returned to the donor without delay.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: If political office holders want to retain a gift, they will have to pay the Government for it at the valuation price.

sections.label: Ridout Road and Iswaran disclosures
sections.summary: The Prime Minister directed CPIB to investigate Ridout Road on 17 May, six days before a statement omitting that, and there is disquiet over a CPIB statement on 12 July omitting Iswaran's arrest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What the Prime Minister did not tell the public but was made known by way of a statement from the Prime Minister's Office written in the third person on 28 June was that the Prime Minister had directed the CPIB to investigate the Ridout Road matter on 17 May – a full six days before his 23 May statement that omitted to mention that he had ordered a CPIB investigation into two of his Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, there is considerable public disquiet about the CPIB releasing a statement on 12 July, which stated that Minister Iswaran was assisting with investigations while omitting to disclose the fact that Minister Iswaran had been arrested a day before.

sections.label: TraceTogether data disclosure delay
sections.summary: The PAP Government took almost nine months to disclose that the SPF sought TraceTogether data for a May 2020 investigation while asserting it was only for contact tracing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The PAP Government took almost nine months before it disclosed to Singaporeans that the Singapore Police Force (SPF) sought to collect TraceTogether data for an investigation in May 2020, even as the PAP continued to assert right through the rest of the year that TraceTogether was only to be used for contact tracing.

sections.label: Tan Chuan-Jin committee and trips
sections.summary: The question asks why Speaker Tan and Cheng Li Hui were on the House Committee after GE 2020 and how many taxpayer-funded foreign trips they took.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My question is if the Prime Minister knew of the affair in 2020, why were Speaker Tan and Cheng Li Hui allowed to be on the same Standing Select Committee of Parliament, namely the House Committee, after GE 2020, when the Prime Minister was already aware of the affair?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, has the Prime Minister checked, since he knew of the affair in 2020, how many foreign trips have both Speaker Tan Chuan-Jin and Cheng Li Hui have been on – at the taxpayers' expense – and was he not aware of them?

sections.label: Tan Chuan-Jin affair handling compared
sections.summary: The question asks how the Tan Chuan-Jin affair differed from Michael Palmer's, what steps were taken for Marine Parade residents, and why he was not asked to step down as Speaker first.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Prime Minister please elaborate how the Tan Chuan-Jin affair with an MP was different from the circumstances and conditions of former PAP Speaker Michael Palmer's affair with a People's Association (PA) member, which Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean then had said, had to be dealt with, I quote, "decisively".

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In other cases of resignations of PAP MPs, such as Michael Palmer, President Halimah, David Ong and Senior Minister Tharman, nothing close to that length of time was required.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could the Prime Minister detail for us what exact steps were taken between February and July 2023 to arrange for the care of Marine Parade residents?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If that was the crux of the issue, then even if the planning for the care of Marine Parade residents was a proper justification for Tan Chuan-Jin to remain a Marine Parade MP for five months, why was he not asked to step down as Speaker first and a new Speaker elected?

sections.label: Counselling of Tan and Cheng
sections.summary: The question asks how Tan Chuan-Jin and Cheng Li Hui were counselled immediately after the Prime Minister was informed about the affair in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How were Tan Chuan-Jin and Cheng Li Hui counselled immediately after Prime Minister was informed about the affair in 2020?

sections.label: CPIB investigation reasons
sections.summary: The CPIB does not investigate somebody unless there is a very serious reason to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: As for CPIB statements, the CPIB does not investigate somebody unless there is a very serious reason to do so.

sections.label: CPIB investigations and prerogative
sections.summary: Minister Chan Chun Sing explained why the CPIB generally does not announce investigations, and the speaker says asking the CPIB to investigate is his prerogative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: If you had listened to Minister Chan Chun Sing, you would have heard that explained very clearly why, in general, the CPIB does not announce any investigations at all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And when I asked the CPIB to investigate, it is my prerogative, I do not have to tell anybody.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: What is important is that I did conduct an investigation and these investigation results were published.

sections.label: Marine Parade move timing
sections.summary: Marine Parade was considered, but the speaker says they should have moved earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: Marine Parade was a consideration, but all things considered, I should have moved earlier.

sections.label: Tan Chuan-Jin overseas trips
sections.summary: Since the last General Election, former Speaker Tan Chuan-Jin went on five official overseas trips and three working trips.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Since the last General Election, former Speaker Mr Tan Chuan-Jin, had gone on five official overseas trips and three working trips.

sections.label: Prime Minister TraceTogether statement
sections.summary: The Prime Minister made a Statement after the TraceTogether debate, in March 2021, where he apologised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: There are matters for which questions still arise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I think the Prime Minister made a Statement well after the TraceTogether issue was debated in Parliament, I think this was in March 2021, where he apologised and said, let me quote, I have to be very clear about this matter.

sections.label: TraceTogether police powers admission
sections.summary: The app was for contact tracing, but Police can ask for information under law; this was not said upfront.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The app was made for contact tracing, but under the law, the Police have powers to ask for information for criminal investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: We should have said so upfront; we did not, and we came out and said so." I must say this statement came after the storm of TraceTogether had passed; and that just reinforces the earlier point that I spoke of.

sections.label: Committee and word rape
sections.summary: The Committee was sensitive about not describing what happened to Ms Khan, but Mr Singh insisted on the word rape.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: My recollection, and he will correct me if I am wrong and there are others here who were in that Committee, was that the Committee was very sensitive about not describing what exactly happened to Ms Khan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But it was Mr Singh who insisted that the word "rape" ought to be mentioned.

sections.label: Ms Khan told leaders of lie
sections.summary: In August, Ms Khan told Mr Singh, Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Faisal Manap she had lied in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Second, what was the point in relation to Ms Khan?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: It was that in August, Mr Singh, Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Faisal Manap were told by her that she had lied in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: She says Mr Singh told her to take it to her grave.

sections.label: Rape mention and mental condition
sections.summary: The speaker says the Committee did not need to mention rape, but Mr Singh insisted on it and on her mental condition.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the first, I think the Leader has missed the point.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I believe the Committee suggested that we do not need to expressly talk about rape and Mr Singh insisted on talking about rape.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Not only that, he insisted on bringing in her mental condition.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think most observers felt a considerable degree of disquiet at this – attacking a young lady on the basis of her mental condition and also insisting on putting on record that she had been raped.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The serious issue was lying in Parliament and then lying again, and that had nothing to do with her sexual assault.

sections.label: Not standing up over lie
sections.summary: The speaker says he did not stand up when she repeated the lie because he had no confirmation she had told her parents about the rape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: It was really a question of why I did not stand up when she repeated the lie.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I had no confirmation as to whether she had dealt with the matter of her rape with her parents.

sections.label: TraceTogether data collection described
sections.summary: TraceTogether temporarily collected Bluetooth proximity data without GPS or movement data, and the data is expunged after 25 days.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We had this extended discussion in early 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But just to refresh your memory, TraceTogether is a system that temporarily collected Bluetooth proximity data without GPS coordinates, without movement data and the data is expunged after 25 days.

sections.label: Section 20 CPC applied
sections.summary: The speaker says he did not know section 20 of the Criminal Procedure Code applied to TraceTogether data when he gave his assurance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: What I had not known when I made the assurance that the data would not be available to law enforcement agencies was that section 20 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC) in fact applied to TraceTogether data, as it does, to all other information which a person may have access to, which the Police may need for the purposes of investigation.

sections.label: January 2021 TraceTogether clarifications
sections.summary: A question was answered on 4 January 2021, and on 5 January 2021 the speaker added clarifications and later indicated legislative changes would come in February 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We did not have a Sitting in December, but I believe it was Mr Christopher de Souza who filed a question.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And on 4 January 2021, the question was answered, I believe, by the Minister of State of Home Affairs, Mr Desmond Tan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: On 5 January 2021, I added further clarifications and I also indicated, I think a few days after that, that we will come back to Parliament in February 2021 with legislative changes to circumscribe the access by law enforcement agencies into TraceTogether data.

sections.label: Timeline of Prime Minister apology
sections.summary: The speaker says the Prime Minister apologised in March, after the issue was dealt with, and describes his own actions from end of October.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I think Minister Shanmugam had a discussion with the Mayor of New York, I believe, talking about privacy concerns, TraceTogether concerns, and my point is, did no one in the Government consider the applicability of section 20 to the CPC?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But what we do know is that the Prime Minister then apologised, not in January, not in February, not in October, November or December, but in March, after we had dealt with the issue and that is my point.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Look at the timeline which I have said, and you have just repeated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I became aware end of — no, I was asked the question by a member of the public, not even in this House, end of October.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I spend November double checking the facts, coordinating, examining the policy options, discussing with my colleagues.

sections.label: Certificate of Urgency obtained
sections.summary: A Certificate of Urgency was needed to make legislative changes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In fact, we had to get a Certificate of Urgency for legislative changes.

sections.label: COP record on Singh wording
sections.summary: The COP record shows Mr Singh saying he was prepared to give the Member time and would use 'sexual assault' if asked.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This is the Committee of Privileges (COP) record.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This is Mr Singh saying, "This is where I think circumstances, in my judgement, were of such a nature that I was prepared to give the Member time, in view of her" – again, I respect what you said earlier, I used the word "rape", but the Committee, in its record, changed it to "sexual assault" and put it in square brackets – "...earlier because this was the word Ms Raeesah Khan used when she described herself, but if Chair and the Committee would want me to use 'sexual assault', I am happy to use that word.

sections.label: Khan on mental illness discredit
sections.summary: Ms Khan said it was extremely out of line for Mr Singh and Ms Lim to use mental illness to discredit her.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Ms Khan said that it was extremely out of line for Mr Singh and Ms Lim to have used mental illness as a means to discredit her.

sections.label: CPC section 20 TraceTogether question
sections.summary: It asks whether the Minister or anyone in MHA raised that section 20 of the CPC applied to TraceTogether before October 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Did the Minister or anybody in the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) ring the bell in Government to say, actually, section 20 of the CPC applies for TraceTogether well before October 2020?

sections.label: CPIB disclosure operational considerations
sections.summary: CPIB's disclosures from 12 July depended on operational considerations and were unrelated to HPL's declaration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The short answers to Dr Tan Wu Meng's questions are as follows: one, would CPIB have revealed more information earlier than what it has done?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As I have explained, what CPIB revealed from 12 July to the subsequent days, is all dependent on its operational considerations – to preserve the integrity of evidence, the confidentiality of the investigations and also not to adversely affect the progress of the investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, what CPIB revealed at any point in time would be CPIB's operational decisions and that has nothing to do with HPL's declaration or otherwise.

sections.label: Iswaran asked to assist investigations
sections.summary: On 11 July, Mr Iswaran was asked to assist in the investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On 12 July, Minister Iswaran was asked to assist in investigations and — sorry, it was on 11 July, Mr Iswaran was asked to assist in the investigation.

sections.label: CPIB investigation and Prime Minister concurrence
sections.summary: A Member asks whether the Prime Minister's concurrence would also be required if CPIB passes a case to the public prosecutor who decides to charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: CPIB has the right to proceed with its investigation.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, to follow up on the point about the Prime Minister's concurrence being sought.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I was just wondering, in the event of an active investigation into a Minister, for example, if the CPIB then decides to pass it on to the public prosecutor, who then decides to proceed, that is, to charge the individual being investigated, would the Primie Minister's concurrence then also be required?

sections.label: CPIB report to AGC
sections.summary: The speaker says he will check an earlier statement, and that once an investigation starts CPIB submits its report to the AGC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Just now, what I said may not be entirely accurate; I will check that and I will get back to the House, as to the hypothetical situation which has not happened, whereby the Prime Minister and the President had not given permission for CPIB to proceed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On Ms He Ting Ru's question, the question is, once the investigation has started, CPIB will submit its report to the AGC and it will be taken to its logical conclusion.

sections.label: Iswaran interdiction and $8,500 pay
sections.summary: A Member asks the Prime Minister to explain the reasoning behind Mr Iswaran receiving $8,500 per month while interdicted from duty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: My second supplementary question, Speaker, is in regards to the Prime Minister's point just now about Mr Iswaran's interdiction from duty, and yet, the Prime Minister mentioned that he would still be getting $8,500 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can the Prime Minister explain the reasoning behind the $8,500?

sections.label: CPIB threshold to name Iswaran
sections.summary: CPIB judged the threshold to say it was talking to Mr Iswaran was there from the beginning because other people would be called in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: In this case, CPIB judged that the threshold to say that they are talking to Mr Iswaran was there right from the beginning, because they were going to call in other people, including Mr Ong Beng Seng, HPL.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: Therefore, it was not possible for this thing to be kept quiet and it had to be stated upfront.

sections.label: President as safeguard over CPIB
sections.summary: If the Prime Minister refuses CPIB consent, CPIB can go to the President, and if the President concurs the Director of CPIB can proceed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And in Singapore, the Prime Minister is in charge and if he is corrupt, you are sunk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: But beyond that, we decided to put in an extra safeguard; and that is, if the Prime Minister directs the CPIB "you do not do that", CPIB can go to the President and say that "Prime Minister has refused me consent, do you concur?" And if the President says yes, then the Director of CPIB can proceed.

sections.label: Reasoning for $8,500 interdiction pay
sections.summary: The speaker says the interdiction and the reason it is $8,500 per month were considered carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: As for the interdiction and why it is $8,500 per month, we considered this carefully.

sections.label: CPIB investigation of Iswaran
sections.summary: CPIB had been working on the Iswaran case since at least May before formal investigations began on 11 July.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: In the case of Mr Iswaran, by the time formal investigations began on 11 July, the CPIB had been working on this case since at least May.

sections.label: Iswaran interdiction and half pay
sections.summary: Iswaran was interdicted and paid $8,500 per month instead of his normal salary, with back pay if innocent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, what is a fair thing to do?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And the Civil Service, their practice is, in such situations, you get interdicted, you are put on half pay, subject to a ceiling and a floor, but you are there until the matter is disposed of.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: If you are, at the end of it, innocent, and nothing is there, your back pay is reinstated to you and made good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: If later on, in fact, you are found guilty, well, at that point, your pay will stop completely and other consequences will follow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I think that is a reasonable model to follow and that is the basis on which I decided that Mr Iswaran will be interdicted and that he will be paid $8,500 per month instead of his normal salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: He was told, acknowledged and that was done.

sections.label: Meal declarations and Iswaran complication
sections.summary: Minister Chan did not answer part (d) of Question No 14 on meal declarations and their total value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Lastly, sorry, I think Minister Chan did not answer part (d) of my Question No 14, which was how many declarations of meals were made in the past year and what was the total value of these declarations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I alerted his Ministers, particularly, in MTI, and we had in mind that this matter was in the background, so that if any issues came up which needed to be decided involving Iswaran, we would know that there was this complication which we would have to think about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: But I did not have a basis yet to suspend him.

sections.label: Tan Chuan-Jin seat and Speaker impartiality
sections.summary: Tan Chuan-Jin's seat did not become vacant in February and he resigned on 17 July.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: As for Mr Tan Chuan-Jin's seat in February, no, it did not become vacant in February.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: In the formal process to resign, he would have had to write to the Deputy Speaker and that is legally done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: That was done when eventually, he did resign, I think, on 17 July.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: Thirdly, on the Speaker being impartial and whether there was a conflict of interest, I addressed this in my main Ministerial Statement just now and explained why this is a situation where it was improper – a Speaker having an affair with an MP.

sections.label: Civil Service convicted zero pay
sections.summary: The Civil Service basis is that if convicted, you are on zero pay and other consequences follow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: The Civil Service works in one way; their basis is if you have been convicted, then you are on zero pay and other consequences will follow.

sections.label: Civil Service half pay decision
sections.summary: The Civil Service says half pay subject to a minimum and ceiling, and $8,500 was decided as much less than half pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: The Civil Service says half pay, subject to a minimum and ceiling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, I decided on this number, $8,500, because much less than half pay.

sections.label: MP allowance not interdicted
sections.summary: The MP's allowance has not been interdicted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: On the MP's allowance, it has not been interdicted.

sections.label: Withholding allowance on suspension
sections.summary: An MP's allowance is withheld once suspended from Parliament's service, under section 29(3) read with section 19 of the Parliament (Privileges, Immunities and Powers) Act 1962.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: An MP's allowance will be withheld once the MP is suspended from the service of Parliament, as provided by section 29(3) read with section 19 of the Parliament (Privileges, Immunities and Powers) Act 1962.

sections.label: CPIB reporting line and oversight
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said CPIB has two keys, the Prime Minister and failing which the President, and a Member asks if the PMO considered extending the reporting line beyond the Executive.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister mentioned earlier that there were two keys for the CPIB: the Prime Minister; and failing which, one could go to the President.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I am wondering if the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) has considered potentially extending this institutional reporting line beyond just essentially one branch of Government, which is the Executive Branch, given that there is also a Judiciary?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In Australia, the National Anti-Corruption Commission is overseen by a joint Select Committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I am very happy to note that Assoc Prof Jamus Lim appreciates the second key and is seeking a third.

sections.label: Safeguards and honest people
sections.summary: The speaker says safeguards and judges exist, cites Lava Jato, and says the solution is honest people with integrity, conviction and courage, not more layers of checks and balances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: You have safeguards; you have got judges involved; but if you have heard of Lava Jato, "Car Wash", it is one of the, what do they call it, the "mother of all corruption scandals"?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, the solution is not to be found in more and more and more and more layers of checks and balances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: The solution is to be found in honest people with integrity, conviction and courage to make the system work with a reasonable degree of redundancy, so I do not have a single point of failure.

sections.label: Code of Conduct sanctions
sections.summary: The Code of Conduct is gazetted today, but the sanctions are not spelled out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today, the Code of Conduct is gazetted, but the sanctions are not spelled out.

sections.label: Leave and CPIB investigation request
sections.summary: That was his personal leave of absence, but on 5 July the Prime Minister and the Government already knew CPIB had requested to investigate him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Yes, okay, that was his personal leave of absence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But on 5 July, the Prime Minister and the Government already knew that CPIB had requested to investigate him.

sections.label: Permission granted to CPIB
sections.summary: They asked for permission on 5 July and permission was given on 6 July.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: They have a good track record and a formidable reputation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: They asked for permission on 5 July; I gave it on 6 July.

sections.label: Investigation started after system worked
sections.summary: It did not get worse and a serious investigation started because the system picked up something wrong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: At some point it may have come out and then we would have a bigger problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: But it did not get worse, and we have started this very serious investigation because our system worked, and we picked up that something was wrong.

sections.label: Backing CPIB investigation of Minister
sections.summary: The speaker told CPIB to do its duty and said Parliament should adopt that attitude.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: Do you think I was pleased when CPIB told me that one of my Ministers needed to be investigated?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I said, "You do your duty; I will back you and I will enable you to do your duty." And I think that is what we, as this Parliament, ought to adopt as our attitude.

sections.label: Tan Chuan-Jin offered to resign
sections.summary: In February Mr Tan Chuan-Jin offered to resign and was told to sort out his constituency first.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: In February, Mr Tan Chuan-Jin told me, "I offer to resign".

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I said, "Yes, sort out your constituency first".

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: The moment to execute it, I will decide.

sections.label: Wrong remark not resignation basis
sections.summary: What he said was wrong, but that alone would not be a basis to ask him to resign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: What he said was wrong, but I would not have considered that alone a basis to ask him to resign.

sections.label: CPIB permission and President route
sections.summary: If the Prime Minister denies CPIB permission, the Director can go to the President, and no Director has been denied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I would say the following things in response to both Ms Lim's comment and, I think, Ms He's question on whether we need permission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, first, if CPIB seeks the Prime Minister's permission and if the Prime Minister denies that, our rule says that the Director of CPIB can go to the President.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And if the President gives his or her approval, CPIB can proceed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The second point is that in our record, over the last many decades, the Director of CPIB has never been denied by the Prime Minister – this Prime Minister or a previous Prime Minister – to continue and proceed with his investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The third point and I have confirmed with the Director of CPIB – when the Prime Minister says no, they can proceed with the investigations and make the case to the President.

sections.label: Driver informant identity protection
sections.summary: The press conference did not address whether steps were taken to protect the driver's identity as an informant, and the driver had secured WP members' phone numbers and circulated the allegation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Nor was there anything in the press conference that addressed the issue of whether steps were taken to protect the driver's identity as an informant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: We made an assessment of the circumstances in which the driver came forward with the information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: There was certain information that I had received after the fact that he had secured the phone numbers of many WP members and circulated this allegation to many members, significant number of members across the board.

sections.label: No corroboratory information available
sections.summary: There was no corroboratory information to work with and no other source.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: What had transpired in terms of what was shared – there was no corroboratory information for us to work with and there was no other source.

sections.label: Minister under CPIB investigation
sections.summary: When a Minister is under investigation, even an informal one for the CPIB to undertake and keep the Prime Minister informed, it is something quite serious.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: What I said was that when a Minister is under investigation and – in this case, it is not just an ordinary investigation – even if it is an informal investigation, for the CPIB to undertake and keep the Prime Minister informed, it is something quite serious.

sections.label: Assurance to Public Service officers
sections.summary: As Minister-in-charge of the Public Service, he assured officers they need not fear if they do their jobs conscientiously, professionally and faithfully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As the Minister-in-charge of the Public Service, I have assured all our Public Service officers that they do not need to fear, as long as they continue to do their jobs conscientiously, professionally and faithfully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I said this during Public Service Week, "Maintain our conviction, uphold our integrity and aspire to the highest standards for Singaporeans and Singapore." So long as they do the right thing, they need not fear, because if they fear or if they start fearing, then this will be the end of the Public Service as we know it today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Our commitment to all Singaporeans is that this Public Service of ours will do right, not just for the short term but also for the long haul.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But if there are things that we need to improve on or work on, we will do so and not hide behind excuses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will continue to do what is right and right what is wrong, because the interests of Singapore and Singaporeans must be at the forefront of everything that we do.
